scenario: AITA for not buying my siblings gifts because they refuse to do a secret Santa? | I have a bunch of siblings, all grown adults, and buying gifts for everyone including parents, partners, and kids is out of control. While I am financially okish, I just can't afford it. Also, neither can my parents and previous years have resulted in my mom being depressed and stressed trying to buy everyone something. Last year, after a some resistance, we agreed to do a secret santa and it went pretty well. Or so I thought. This year 1 sibling threw a fit about doing it. She said she doesn't like "putting rules on holidays" and it's not fair. As a side note, she and our younger siblings rarely buy anyone anything. Last year was the 1st time everyone brought something. Another sibling, who is hosting Christmas, sided with her and said that we won't do a secret Santa but that you don't have to bring gifts if you don't want to. Am an asshole if I don't buy my siblings gifts? I love my family but I can't afford it this year. I was going to get nieces and nephews gifts but that's it.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me not to buy my siblings gifts because they refuse to do a Secret Santa. Let me start by understanding the situation better. I have a bunch of grown-up siblings, and buying gifts for everyone, including parents, partners, and kids, is getting out of control. I'm financially okay, but I just can't afford it this year. My parents also can't afford it, and last year, my mom was really stressed and even got depressed trying to buy everyone something. Last year, after some resistance, we agreed to do a Secret Santa, and it went pretty well, or so I thought. This year, one of my siblings threw a fit about doing it. She said she doesn't like "putting rules on holidays" and that it's not fair. As a side note, she and our younger siblings rarely buy anything for anyone. Last year was the first time everyone brought something. Another sibling, who is hosting Christmas, sided with her and said that we won't do a Secret Santa but that you don't have to bring gifts if you don't want to. I'm feeling stuck because I love my family, but I can't afford to buy gifts for everyone this year. I was planning to get gifts for my nieces and nephews but that's it. I'm wondering if it's right or wrong for me not to buy gifts for my siblings because they refuse to do a Secret Santa. First, I need to consider the reasons behind wanting to do a Secret Santa. It seems like it was a way to make gift-giving more manageable and less stressful, especially since last year my mom was really stressed. Secret Santa can help distribute the gift-giving responsibility more evenly, so no one person is overwhelmed. However, one of my siblings doesn't like the idea of putting rules on holidays, and she feels it's not fair. She and the younger siblings rarely buy anything, which might contribute to the stress of others who are trying to buy gifts for everyone. I also need to think about the financial aspect. I can't afford to buy gifts for everyone, and my parents are in a similar situation. It's important to set boundaries to avoid financial stress, which can affect my well-being and my relationship with my family. On the other hand, not buying gifts for my siblings might make them feel neglected or unappreciated, especially if they are expecting gifts. It's important to communicate my situation honestly and find a middle ground that works for everyone. Maybe instead of a Secret Santa, we can have an open discussion about what everyone can afford and what they are comfortable with. Perhaps we can agree to exchange gifts only with certain people or set a budget limit. It's important to ensure that everyone feels included and valued without causing financial strain. I also need to consider the emotional impact. My mom was stressed last year, and I don't want that to happen again. It's important to create a holiday environment that is joyful and stress-free for everyone. In conclusion, while it might seem like not buying gifts for my siblings is the right decision financially, it's important to communicate and find a solution that works for everyone. It's not just about the money but also about maintaining harmony and ensuring that everyone feels appreciated and included in the holiday celebrations.
